Issues.Title: fix(http): include query params in the XHR backend fallback URL
Issues.Body:
When the browser did not provide a response URL, as happens on network errors and timeouts, HttpXhrBackend fell back on `req.url`, which leaves out the query params. So `HttpErrorResponse.url` and its message showed `/api/items` for a request to `/api/items?page=2`.

Fall back on `req.urlWithParams`, which is the URL the request was sent to and what FetchBackend already uses.

Issues.Title: fix(http): keep the response text when a JSON response fails to parse with fetch
Issues.Body:
When a 2xx response with `responseType: 'json'` could not be parsed, FetchBackend reported the bare `SyntaxError` as `HttpErrorResponse.error`, so the response body was lost. HttpXhrBackend reports `{error, text}` in this case, which lets apps show or log the body (for example an HTML maintenance page returned with status 200).

Report the same `{error, text}` shape from FetchBackend, keeping the original text including any XSSI prefix, as the XHR backend does.

Fixes https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/63250

Issues.Title: compiler: selectorless lexer loops forever on a lowercase "@" attribute (e.g. animation trigger)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes — only since selectorless lexing was added. The same template lexes fine with `selectorlessEnabled: false`. ### Description When `selectorlessEnabled` is on, the HTML lexer never terminates on any `@` inside a start tag that is not followed by `_` or an uppercase letter. `_consumeTagOpen` in `packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts`: ```ts if (this._selectorlessEnabled && this._cursor.peek() === chars.$AT) { const start = this._cursor.clone(); const nameStart = start.clone(); nameStart.advance(); if (isSelectorlessNameStart(nameStart.peek())) { // `_` or A-Z only this._consumeDirective(start, nameStart); } } else { this._consumeAttribute(); } ``` When the character after `@` is a lowercase letter (or a digit, or another `@`), `isSelectorlessNameStart` is `false`, so the `if` body is skipped — and the `else` is not entered, because `peek() === '@'`. Nothing consumes a character, so the enclosing `while (true)` in `_consumeTagOpen` spins forever at 100% CPU. This is reachable from valid templates: `binding_parser.ts` treats any attribute whose name starts with `@` as a legacy animation label (`isLegacyAnimationLabel(name) { return name[0] == '@'; }`), and animation triggers are conventionally lowercase. A selectorless component containing `
` therefore hangs the compiler. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction The same lexer is vendored (slightly modified) in `prettier/angular-html-parser`, where the repro is unambiguous: ```js parse('
', { enableAngularSelectorlessSyntax: true }); // never returns ``` - prettier/angular-html-parser#57 — report + repro - prettier/angular-html-parser#59 — proposed fix A unit test in `packages/compiler/test/ml_parser/lexer_spec.ts` using `{selectorlessEnabled: true}` would hang the test suite (it cannot even fail; it never returns). ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No exception — the process hangs and has to be killed. Reproduced on Node 24 against `@angular/compiler` at `main`. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in - Angular: `main` (`v22.0.0-next`), `packages/compiler` - Node: 24 - OS: Linux ### Anything else? `isSelectorlessNameStart` being `_`/`A-Z` looks intentional (cf. angular/angular#70831, which rejects `` as a lowercase selectorless segment), so the fix is **not** to accept lowercase selectorless names. The `@` branch should fall back to `_consumeAttribute()` when it cannot start a directive — which is exactly what the lexer already does when `selectorlessEnabled` is `false`. That keeps `
` a plain attribute instead of erroring, and makes the loop always advance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "compiler: selectorless lexer loops forever on a lowercase "@" attribute (e.g. animation trigger)" (#71324)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): don't hang on a lowercase "@" attribute in selectorless tags
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? Issue Number: #71324 With `selectorlessEnabled`, the attribute loop in `_consumeTagOpen` only consumed `@` when it was followed by a selectorless name start (`_` or an uppercase letter, i.e. a PascalCase component/directive reference). Any other `@` — a lowercase animation trigger such as `@fadeIn`, or a lone `@` — matched neither branch, so the cursor never advanced and the lexer looped forever at 100% CPU. This is reachable from valid templates: `binding_parser.ts` treats any attribute whose name starts with `@` as a legacy animation label (`isLegacyAnimationLabel`), and animation triggers are conventionally lowercase, so a selectorless component containing `
` hangs the compiler. ## What is the new behavior? The `@` branch falls through to `_consumeAttribute()` when it cannot start a directive — which is exactly what the lexer already does when selectorless syntax is disabled. `@fadeIn` stays an ordinary attribute, `@MyDir` is still a directive, and the loop always advances. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information `isSelectorlessNameStart` staying `_`/`A-Z` looks intentional (cf. #70831, which rejects `` as a lowercase selectorless segment), so this deliberately does not start accepting lowercase selectorless names.

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

## What is the current behavior?

Newer versions of Chromium implement the experimental WICG HTML-in-Canvas specification, adding an `onpaint` property descriptor to `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype`.

The test `should patch all possible on properties on element` creates `<canvas>` and asserts against all known event names (including `paint` from `windowEventNames`). Because zone.js does not patch `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype`, the test fails on newer Chromium with:
`Failed: onpaint of [object HTMLCanvasElement] is not patched`.

## What is the new behavior?

`onpaint` is ignored in `should patch all possible on properties on element`, aligning with `onorientationchange`. Since zone.js is in maintenance mode and `onpaint` is an experimental API, zone.js does not monkey-patch this property.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): implement extended template diagnostics in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
Stacked on top of #71313.

### Summary
Implements AST-only and scope-aware extended template diagnostics in the NGP (`packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor`) pipeline:

- **Extended Template Diagnostics (`ExtendedTemplateChecker`)**:
  - `deferTriggerMisconfiguration` (`NG8021`)
  - `invalidBananaInBox` (`NG8101`)
  - `missingControlFlowDirective` (`NG8103`)
  - `textAttributeNotBinding` (`NG8104`)
  - `missingNgForOfLet` (`NG8105`)
  - `suffixNotSupported` (`NG8106`)
  - `skipHydrationNotStatic` (`NG8108`)
  - `uninvokedFunctionInEventBinding` (`NG8111` — inline arrow/function expressions)
  - `unusedLetDeclaration` (`NG8112`)
  - `unparenthesizedNullishCoalescing` (`NG8114`)
  - `missingStructuralDirective` (`NG8116`)
- **Template Variable Write Semantics (`checkTemplateVariableWrites`)**:
  - Detects illegal writes to `@let`, `@for`, and template `#ref` / `let-` variables (`NG8005`).
- **Unused Standalone Imports (`checkUnusedStandaloneImports`)**:
  - Tracks resolved `@Component.imports` entries and spans in `ng-analyze` (Rust) and emits `NG8113` diagnostics for unused standalone imports in `tcb.ts`.
- **Configuration Validation (`verifyExtendedDiagnosticsOptions`)**:
  - Validates `extendedDiagnostics` option compatibility (`strictTemplates` requirement, `defaultCategory`, and `checks` names/categories).
- **Shared Test Suite Updates**:
  - Updates `ngp_typecheck_testing.ts` and removes newly passing tests from `NGP_KNOWN_EXTENDED_CHECK_FAILURES` and `NGP_KNOWN_NGTSC_FAILURES`.

Issues.Title: docs: fix the default of preserveContent in the aria accordion and tabs guides
Issues.Body:
The aria accordion and tabs guides had the `preserveContent` default backwards. They said panel content stays in the DOM unless you set `[preserveContent]="false"`.

The input actually defaults to `false`, so lazy content (the stuff inside `ngAccordionContent` or `ngTabContent`) gets destroyed when the panel closes. Setting it to `true` is what keeps it around, which is why the tabs examples already do that.

This fixes both sentences and says which content they apply to.

### [`v5.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/blob/HEAD/History.md#530)

#### 🐞 Bug fixes

- Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by [@​YuryShkoda](https://redirect.github.com/YuryShkoda) in [#​4893](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4893)

  Fixed the behavior of `res.send()` to prevent conflicts between `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` HTTP headers in responses. The `Content-Length` header in `res.send()` is now only added when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a `Transfer-Encoding` header - by [@​cuishuang](https://redirect.github.com/cuishuang) in [#​7459](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7459)

* Upgrade `qs` to `^6.16.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-2391](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-2391) ([GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883](https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/security/advisories/GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883)), [CVE-2026-82417](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82417) ([GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g)) and [CVE-2026-82562](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82562) ([GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx)): `arrayLimit` bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled `isBuffer` - by [@​davetashner](https://redirect.github.com/davetashner) in [#​7057](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7057) and [#​7478](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7478), and [@​cyphercodes](https://redirect.github.com/cyphercodes) in [#​7305](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7305)

* Upgrade `proxy-addr` to `^2.0.8`, which fixes [CVE-2026-90711](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90711) - by [@​lazerg](https://redirect.github.com/lazerg) in [#​7474](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7474)

#### 🚀 Improvements

- Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. `req.fresh` previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by [@​Cherry](https://redirect.github.com/Cherry) in [#​7366](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7366)

  ```js
  // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
  app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
    res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
    res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
  });
  ```

- Improve HTML structure in `res.redirect()` responses when HTML format is accepted by adding `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` tags for better browser compatibility - by [@​Bernice55231](https://redirect.github.com/Bernice55231) in [#​5167](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/5167)

- When calling `app.render` with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by [AkaHarshit](https://redirect.github.com/AkaHarshit) in [#​6903](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6903)

  ```js
  app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected
  ```

- Upgrade `content-type` to `^2.0.0`, bringing a faster parser (\~1.5x quicker `Content-Type` parsing/formatting in `res.send()`) along with a behavior change: `res.send()` now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a `Content-Type` that fails to parse. `type-is` is upgraded to `^2.1.0` as part of the same change - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7234](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7234)

  ```js
  res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
  // -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8
  ```

- The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as `Error.cause` and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's `parent`/`original`) are no longer swallowed - by [@​Nitin-Mohapatra](https://redirect.github.com/Nitin-Mohapatra) in [#​6464](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6464)

- Upgrade `content-disposition` to `^2.0.1`, which changes the `Content-Disposition` header emitted by `res.download()`, `res.attachment()`, and `res.sendFile()`: file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7233](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7233)

  ```js
  res.attachment('user.html');
  // before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
  // after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html
  ```

- Upgrade `body-parser` to `^2.3.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-12590](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12590) ([GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)): an invalid `limit` option value caused request body size enforcement to be silently disabled (fail-open), allowing a denial of service via arbitrarily large payloads. Invalid `limit` values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by [@​Mayvis](https://redirect.github.com/Mayvis) in [#​7390](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7390)

### [`v12.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.1): pnpm 12.11.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.0...v12.11.1)

This release fixes two ways `pnpm install` could fail, runs tools of any Rust release through `pnx`, and treats `registry.npmjs.com` as an alias of the npm registry.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install` no longer fails when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version. pnpm warns and continues. A registry mirror that has not synced a release no longer blocks the commands of a project pinned to it.

- `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD` when `node_modules/.bin` holds a shim that another user created, if everyone can already execute it and it is not world-writable. This happens when several users share one checkout.

- `enable-modules-dir=false` (`enableModulesDir: false` through the Node.js addon) fetches the registry packages the host can install into the store again, as pnpm v10 did, while still writing nothing under `node_modules`. The setting exists for a `node_modules` that something else mounts from the store, such as a FUSE daemon, and that consumer no longer has to download each package on first access. A plain `--lockfile-only` run still fetches nothing.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer put `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` files in the tarball. A `files` entry that names one still ships it.

- pnpm now treats `https://registry.npmjs.com/` as an alias of `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Registry requests, credentials, and trusted publishing use the canonical hostname.

- `pnx --package=rust@<channel> <tool>` runs a tool of that Rust release, for example `pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-01-01 cargo build`. pnpm installs the release with the components and targets from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the target of each `--target` argument.

- `pnpm install` now links agent skills for more coding agents. It detects the agent from `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `AI_AGENT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE` [pnpm/tasks#116](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/116).

- When the registry rejects `pnpm stage publish`, the error message now starts with "Failed to stage package".

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #34335

`findTests` returns the test files in the order `tinyglobby` yields them. The glob crawls directories asynchronously, so the order changes between runs: on a project with 255 spec files, 8 consecutive calls returned 8 different orders (same set of files). That order feeds the build entry points and `rootFiles`, so two `ng test` builds of the same sources produce different chunks: imports come out reordered, the content-hashed chunk names change, and the change cascades to every importer (79 to 89 of 593 output files renamed between two runs). This defeats Vitest 5's `fsModuleCache`, which is keyed on file content.

## What is the new behavior?

The discovered test files are sorted before being turned into entry points. With that change, three consecutive builds of the same project produced byte-identical test bundles (0 of 593 files differing, `--dump-virtual-files` output compared with `diff -r`), and Vitest's module cache was fully reused across runs.

A `findTests` spec checks the result is sorted. The crawl order can happen to be sorted on a small fixture, so it guards against a regression rather than reproducing the race on every run.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Measured with `@angular/build` 22.2.2, Vitest 5.0.4, Node 24, on macOS; the same non-determinism shows up in AOT and JIT test builds, with and without `--coverage`, and with `NG_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS=1`.

Issues.Title: unit-test builder (Vitest): test bundle output is not deterministic, which defeats Vitest 5 `fsModuleCache`
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Building the same project twice in a row with `@angular/build:unit-test` (Vitest runner), with no source change in between, produces different output files: the same modules end up with different chunk names, because the import statements inside some chunks and spec entry points come out in a different order.

Only the order changes, never the code. Normalising the chunk names (`chunk-[A-Z0-9]{8}` → `chunk-X`) and comparing the files, every difference is one of:

- side-effect imports reordered in a spec entry point:
  ```diff
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  ```
- named imports moved between two `import { … } from "./chunk-X.js"` statements:
  ```diff
  +import {
  +  SomeMapper
  +} from "./chunk-X.js";
   ...
  -import {
  -  SomeMapper
  -} from "./chunk-X.js";
  ```
- identifiers swapped in a re-exported list (`ModuleA, ModuleB` → `ModuleB, ModuleA`).

Since the chunk file names are content hashes, one reordered chunk renames itself and, in cascade, every chunk or spec that imports it.

Measured on two applications of the same workspace (two consecutive `ng test <app> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`):

| project | JS files in the test bundle | files renamed between two runs |
|---|---|---|
| app A, JIT test build (`aot: false`) | 593 | 79 to 89 |
| app B, JIT test build | 89 | 10 |
| app B, AOT (default `build:development`) | 88 | 18 |
| two small libraries | 9 and 11 | 0 |

It happens with and without `--coverage`, in AOT and JIT, and with `NG_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS=1`, so it does not look like a worker race in the Angular compilation.

**Why it matters.** Vitest 5 enables `fsModuleCache` by default and keys it on file content and id. With the builder's output changing between runs, part of the cache is invalidated on every run (about 20 % of the entries for app A), so the cache cannot be reused between CI pipelines. Disabling `splitting` makes the output stable (100 % cache reuse) but the option is deprecated ("No longer needed with Vitest 5") and the suite is much slower without shared chunks (app A with coverage, warm cache: ~45 s instead of ~30 s).

Expected: identical inputs give byte-identical test bundles, as they would for a reproducible build.

### Minimal Reproduction

Not yet reduced to a public repository. Any workspace whose specs share enough code to produce many shared chunks should show it:

1. `ng test <project> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`
2. Copy `.angular/cache/<version>/<project>/unit-test/output-files` aside.
3. Run step 1 again, without touching anything.
4. Compare the two lists of `*.js` file names: some chunk names differ. Diffing a renamed chunk against its counterpart only shows reordered imports.

Small projects (around ten output files) do not show it in our workspace.

### Exception or Error

_No response_

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64 (on the node:24-alpine CI image, the persisted Vitest cache also grows on every pipeline instead of being reused)

@angular/build    : 22.2.2
vitest            : 5.0.4
esbuild           : 0.28.2
```

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): resolve unimported NgModule scopes when filtering unit-test files
Issues.Body:
When `rootFiles` overrides are provided (such as during `unit-test` runs), the initial TypeScript program is restricted to those entry points and their transitive imports. If a test imports a non-standalone `@Component` directly without importing its declaring `@NgModule`, the `NgModule` may be omitted from the program and leave the component without its compilation scope.

Preserve the full `tsconfig` root file set as `fallbackRootNames` for application builds when `rootFiles` is a subset of the `tsconfig` files. If AOT analysis detects a non-standalone component lacking an owning `NgModule` scope (`getOwningNgModule(component) === null`) and additional uncompiled `tsconfig` files exist, recreate and re-analyze the Angular program with the full root file set so all `NgModule` declarations can be discovered.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): preserve preload metadata for nested empty-path routes
Issues.Body:
Previously, `handleRoute` yielded a parent route's metadata before appending `loadChildren` preloads or traversing child routes, while `traverseRoutesConfig` appended a trailing slash only to empty-path routes. Under a non-empty parent, the parent ('/pricing') and its empty-path child ('/pricing/') received distinct keys during `getRoutesFromAngularRouterConfig` deduplication (`seenRoutes`) and were only merged later by `RouteTree.insert`. However, when an empty-path route was nested under another empty-path route (such as at the root '/' or under '/es' -> '' -> ''), both the parent and child received the same key, causing `seenRoutes` to keep the outer route's metadata and drop the descendant's accumulated `preload` and redirect metadata.

Update `handleRoute` to append `loadChildren` preloads upfront and allow the first matching empty-path child route to override its parent's metadata for the same path, and remove the redundant `addTrailingSlash` keying in `traverseRoutesConfig`.

Closes #34320

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): keep Vite server file watcher disabled in Vitest watch mode
Issues.Body:
In Vitest 5, the internal `vitest:config:append` plugin uses a post `configResolved` hook that resets `server.watch` to `{}` when watch mode is enabled (`server.watch ??= {}`), overriding the `server: { watch: null }` setting passed in `vitestServerConfig`. This caused Vite to start a duplicate Chokidar file watcher alongside the Angular CLI build watcher and trigger redundant, racing test reruns on file changes.

Enforce `post` ordering on `angular:vitest-configuration` and reset `config.server.watch = null` in a post `configResolved` hook so Vite uses its no-op watcher.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): ensure Sass importers return global Promise instances
Issues.Body:
`sass-embedded` checks whether an importer's `canonicalize` method returned a promise using `result instanceof Promise`. When SSR executes in the same process during `ng serve` for an application using Zone.js, `zone.js/node` replaces `globalThis.Promise` with `ZoneAwarePromise`. Because native V8 `async` functions always return instances of the intrinsic V8 `%Promise%` rather than `globalThis.Promise`, `result instanceof Promise` evaluates to `false` and `sass-embedded` treats the returned Promise as a synchronous URL value (`"[object Promise]"` / `"%5Bobject%20Promise%5D"`).

Use `Promise.resolve(...)` instead of a native `async` method in `AsyncModuleUrlRebasingImporter.canonicalize` so the returned promise is constructed via the active `globalThis.Promise`.

Closes #34309

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): resolve parameters in redirect targets
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Follow-up to https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34301#issuecomment-6098158362.

Parameters in a `redirectTo` target are sent unchanged in the server's `Location` header, while the router replaces them:

| Route | Request | Server `Location` | Router navigates to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user/:id` → `profile/:id` | `/user/7` | `/profile/:id` | `/profile/7` |
| `search/:term` → `/find?q=:x` | `/search/cats?x=dogs` | `/find?q=:x` | `/find?q=dogs` |

## What is the new behavior?

The server resolves both, one commit each:

1. **Route parameters:** during route extraction, `:name` in the redirect path becomes `*<n>`, the position of that parameter in the request path, which `buildPathWithParams` resolves at request time. Prerendered routes get the value from `getPrerenderParams`.
2. **Query placeholders of absolute redirects:** `q=:x` takes the values of `x` from the request query.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Without `x` in the request, the server redirects to `/find`. The router would go to `/find?q=undefined`.

Issues.Title: @angular/ssr: page under nested empty-path routes is prerendered without the modulepreload hints of its lazy chunks (regression since 19.1.6)
Issues.Body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: 19.1.5 ### Description A prerendered page reached through an empty-path route nested under another empty-path route (a componentless `''` route whose `''` child is a `loadChildren`, whose own `''` route is a `loadComponent`) is emitted without any `` hint for its own lazy chunks. A sibling page reached through a non-empty path with exactly the same lazy depth (`'pricing'` → `loadChildren` → `''` `loadComponent`) gets both of its hints. The page itself renders correctly; only the hints are missing. Measured with 22.2.2, `outputMode: "static"` (`index.csr.html` has 0 hints): | Routes | `/` | `/pricing` | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | `''` (componentless) → `''` loadChildren → `''` loadComponent | **0** (expected 2: `home.routes`, `home-page`) | 2 (`pricing.routes`, `pricing-page`) | | home flattened to a top-level `''` loadComponent | 1 (`home-page`, its only chunk) | 2 | Same nested routes on 19.1.5 vs 19.1.6 (both builds share 2 initial chunks, which `index.csr.html` also has): | Version | `/` | `/pricing` | | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------- | | 19.1.5 | 4 (2 shared + `home.routes` + `home-page`) | 4 | | 19.1.6 | **2** (shared only) | 4 | | `@angular/ssr` 19.1.5 with `@angular/build` 19.1.6 | 4 | 4 | The chunk hashes are identical across these builds; only `@angular/ssr` makes the difference. **Likely cause** (`packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts`): `traverseRoutesConfig` keys an empty-path route as `addTrailingSlash(currentRoutePath)`. Under a non-empty parent the parent and its `''` child get different keys (`/pricing` and `/pricing/`), which `RouteTree.insert` later merges with the last entry winning, the leaf that carries the accumulated `preload`. Under an empty-path parent both get the same key (`/`, or `/es/` for `es` → `''` → `''`), and `getRoutesFromAngularRouterConfig` keeps only the first result per key (`seenRoutes`, added in 5bf5e5fd2 "fix(@angular/ssr): prioritize the first matching route over subsequent ones", #29539). The first result is the outer route, yielded before `handleRoute` appends its `loadChildren` preloads and before any descendant's `loadComponent` preloads, so the leaf's metadata with the preloads is dropped. That dedupe is right for competing sibling routes with the same path; here the later entry is a descendant in the same match chain, the route the router actually activates. **Expected:** the prerendered page carries the hints of the route chain that renders it, as on 19.1.5 (for example, let a later result replace the kept one, or merge its `preload`, when it is a descendant of it rather than a sibling). **Real-world impact:** our home page had 3 modulepreload hints against 12 on `/pricing`; flattening the home route to a top-level `loadComponent` gave 9. ### Minimal Reproduction ```bash npx -p @angular/cli@22.2.2 ng new repro --ssr --routing --style=css --skip-git --skip-tests --defaults --ai-config=none --package-manager=npm cd repro # angular.json: set "outputMode": "static" # src/app/app.html: replace its content with (optional, only trims the placeholder) # app.routes.server.ts stays as generated: [{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender }] ``` `src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', children: [ { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: () => import('./home/home.routes') }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: () => import('./pricing/pricing.routes') }, ], }, ]; ``` `src/app/home/home.routes.ts` (and `src/app/pricing/pricing.routes.ts`, the same with `./pricing-page`) ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export default [{ path: '', loadComponent: () => import('./home-page') }] satisfies Routes; ``` `src/app/home/home-page.ts` (and `src/app/pricing/pricing-page.ts`, the same with `PricingPage`) ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ template: '

Home page

' }) export default class HomePage {} ``` ```bash npx ng build grep -o ']*>' dist/repro/browser/index.html # nothing grep -o ']*>' dist/repro/browser/pricing/index.html # 2 links ``` Workaround that brings `/` back to its hint, the page as a top-level route: ```ts export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadComponent: () => import('./home/home-page') }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: () => import('./pricing/pricing.routes') }, ]; ``` ### Exception or Error ```text None. The build succeeds ("Prerendered 2 static routes.") and both pages render their content; only the modulepreload hints of `/` are missing. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.2 Angular : 22.2.2 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 @angular/build 22.2.2 @angular/cli 22.2.2 @angular/common 22.2.2 @angular/compiler 22.2.2 @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.2 @angular/core 22.2.2 @angular/forms 22.2.2 @angular/platform-browser 22.2.2 @angular/platform-server 22.2.2 @angular/router 22.2.2 @angular/ssr 22.2.2 rxjs 7.8.2 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else relevant? - At the root, one empty-path level under another is enough: a top-level `{ path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: () => import('./home/home.routes') }` with no componentless wrapper also gives `/` 0 hints. So removing only the wrapper is not a workaround; the page itself must be the top-level `''` route. - Not specific to the root: `{ path: 'es', children: [{ path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: ... }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: ... }] }` gives `/es` 0 hints and `/es/pricing` 2. - The per-route `preload` feature itself worked in 19.1.0–19.1.5; the `seenRoutes` dedupe appears in 19.1.6 and is still there in 22.2.2.

Issues.Title: `ng serve` crashes with `EMFILE: too many open files, watch` on macOS when `preserveSymlinks` is enabled (22.2 regression)
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.1.9

### Description

Since 22.2.0, `ng serve` (and any watch build) crashes on macOS right after the first successful build when the build target sets `preserveSymlinks: true` and the workspace contains more than 4096 directories outside `node_modules`.

`setupWatcher` passes `preserveSymlinks` on as `followSymlinks`, and `createWatcher` then always picks chokidar over `@parcel/watcher`:

```js
if (options?.polling || options?.followSymlinks) {
  return createChokidarWatcher(options);
}
```

Chokidar 5 calls `fs.watch` once per directory and file under the workspace root. On macOS, Node reports `EMFILE` as soon as one process holds more than 4096 directory watches: 4096 `fs.watch` calls on directories work, 4097 fail. File watches do not count towards this (50,000 worked), and `ulimit -n` has no influence: the crash reproduces with the hard limit at `unlimited`.

The error is emitted on the `FSWatcher` without a listener, so the dev server process exits.

In our application (about 1,250 source directories plus the packages it imports from `node_modules`, which chokidar also watches whole) the dev server made 33,703 `fs.watch` calls before crashing. With 22.1.9 and watchpack the same workspace needs 4. We depend on `preserveSymlinks` because plugin frontends are symlinked into `src/`.

### Minimal Reproduction

On macOS:

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2 new emfile-repro --defaults --skip-git
cd emfile-repro
node -e "for (let i = 0; i < 4200; i++) fs.mkdirSync('many/d' + i, { recursive: true })"
npx ng config projects.emfile-repro.architect.build.options.preserveSymlinks true
npx ng serve
```

The server prints its local URL and exits a moment later with the error below. It keeps running with `preserveSymlinks` unset, or with 3000 directories instead of 4200.

### Exception or Error

```text
Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:267:21)
Emitted 'error' event on FSWatcher instance at:
    at FSWatcher._handleError (node_modules/chokidar/index.js:558:18)
    at NodeFsHandler._boundHandleError (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:297:49)
    at node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:144:9
    at foreach (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:76:9)
    at fsWatchBroadcast (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:143:5)
    at FSWatcher.<anonymous> (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:191:17)
    at FSWatcher.emit (node:events:509:28)
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:273:12) {
  errno: -24,
  syscall: 'watch',
  code: 'EMFILE',
  filename: null
}
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64 (macOS 27.0.1)

@angular/build            22.2.2
@angular/cli              22.2.2
@angular/compiler-cli     22.2.2
typescript                6.0.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

`@parcel/watcher` loads and subscribes fine on the same machine, so this is not the load-failure fallback. With `preserveSymlinks` off the dev server holds no `fs.watch` handles at all. Would it be possible to keep the parcel watcher for `preserveSymlinks` workspaces, or to limit chokidar to the files the build actually reports instead of the whole workspace root?

Workaround: pin `@angular/build` to 22.1.9, or run with `--watch false`.

Issues.Title: bug(mat-datepicker): date parse errors are not propagated to Signal Forms
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

The datepicker input provides a matDatepickerParse validation error when the user enters text that cannot be parsed as a date.

This error is available when using Reactive Forms, but when using Signal Forms, the error does not reach the errors signal of the field tree. The value of the form field stays as `null`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-d3y2q7gw?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the application.
2. Enter an invalid date string into the Reactive Forms datepicker.
3. Observe that the control reports a matDatepickerParse error.
4. Enter the same invalid date string into the Signal Forms datepicker.
5. Observe that the Signal Forms field does not report the corresponding parse error in field().errors().

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the date parse errors to also be available to the Signal Form.

If I understand correctly, this seems to be in line with the direction of the Angular Signal Forms API, for example with https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/transformedValue to report parse errors in custom controls.

### Actual Behavior

The date parse errors are not available to the Signal Form. Since the form value remains as `null` for invalid values, distinguishing between an empty form and invalid input is not possible in the schema.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.2
- CDK/Material: 22.2.2
- Browser(s): Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33740.

When a datepicker input is bound to a signal form with `[formField]`, the `matDatepickerParse` error goes stale whenever the model value stays `null`:

- typing an unparseable value (e.g. `foo`) into an empty input does not add the error;
- erasing an unparseable value does not clear it, so the form stays invalid on an empty field (the case in the issue).

## Cause

Signal forms compute the errors of a CVA's legacy validators in a `computed` that re-runs when the control value changes or when the validator calls its `registerOnValidatorChange` callback. In `MatDatepickerInputBase._onInput()`, the `null` to `null` path calls `_cvaOnChange(null)`, which signal forms ignore because the value did not change, and it never calls `_validatorOnChange()`: that call was only in the branch for a non-null, unchanged date. Reactive forms don't hit this, because `setValue` always re-runs the validators.

## Fix

Call `_validatorOnChange()` whenever the parse state flips while the value stays the same, including `null` to `null`. The branch that already did this for an unchanged non-null date behaves as before.

With reactive forms, the `null` to `null` case with a changed parse state now also triggers `updateValueAndValidity()` after the `setValue(null)` call. It gives the same result, with one extra `valueChanges`/`statusChanges` emission in that case.

## Testing

Two tests in `datepicker.spec.ts` use a real signal form (`form()` + `FormField`). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- typing `foo` into an empty input sets `matDatepickerParse`;
- setting a date, typing `foo`, then clearing the input removes it.

`//src/material/datepicker:unit_tests_chromium` (407 tests, including the date range input) and `//src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium` pass locally.

Issues.Title: bug(COMPONENT): Angular ARIA tab must allow eager loading of tab content
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

## Description

Angular Aria's tabs implementation appears to require tab panel content to be declared using `ng-template[ngTabContent]`, which prevents consumers from eagerly rendering tab panel content in the DOM.

This is problematic for use cases where all tab panels need to be initialized upfront, rather than lazily instantiated when their associated tabs become active. For example, a tab panel may contain a component that needs to initialize early, or preload data that is required for SEO (in SSR setup).

Currently, `ngTabContent` can only be applied to an `ng-template`, and the implementation warns when a tab panel does not contain the expected content directive. Applying `ngTabContent` directly to a component or a regular element does not work because it does not match the directive's selector.

It would be useful to provide a supported way to eagerly instantiate tab panel content while retaining the existing tab panel API and accessibility behavior.

## Reasoning

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide recommends automatic tab activation on focus when the associated panel can be displayed without noticeable latency. It also notes that this typically requires panel content to be preloaded; otherwise, automatic activation introduces delays that significantly hinder efficient keyboard navigation.

Eager loading is therefore a legitimate use case for accessible tabs, particularly when panel content requires initialization or data fetching before it can be displayed.

Providing an explicit mechanism for eager content instantiation would allow developers to avoid unnecessary delays during tab navigation without having to implement their own tab behavior or work around the current content directive requirements.

### Reproduction

Link: https://angular.dev/guide/aria/tabs#example-1



### Expected Behavior

I expect the ngTabContent to have a selector on its own without the ng-template infront, so that the tab content can be eagerly loaded

### Actual Behavior

The ngTabContent selector has ng-template in front of it which prevents us from eagerly loading tab content that may contain useful information and is needed upfront and without layout shift

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: N/A
- Browser(s): latest
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A

Issues.Title: fix(google-maps): avoid inline host style that violates CSP style-src
Issues.Body:
## What

`MapInfoWindow` hides its host element with `host: {'style': 'display: none'}`. This renders as an inline `style` attribute on `<map-info-window>`, which is blocked by a Content Security Policy whose `style-src` doesn't include `'unsafe-inline'`. The browser reports a violation like this for every info window on the page:

> Applying inline style violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'style-src ...'

## Fix

Remove the host style binding and set `display: none` on the host element in the constructor through CSSOM (`element.style.display`). CSP doesn't block CSSOM assignments, so the behavior is unchanged and the directive works under a strict `style-src`.

## Testing

Verified in an app running a strict CSP (`style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'`): before the change, each `<map-info-window>` raised a CSP violation; after it, none are raised, and the info windows still open and close normally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(google-maps): avoid inline host style that violates CSP style-src" (#33947)

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/text-field): cdkTextareaAutosize caches line height before matInput applies `font: inherit`, so min/max rows are wrong
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

14.x (verified on v14.material.angular.dev, Angular 14.0.0)

### Description

When `cdkTextareaAutosize` is used on a `matInput` textarea inside `mat-form-field`, the cached line height used for `cdkAutosizeMinRows` / `cdkAutosizeMaxRows` is measured with the browser's default textarea font instead of the form field's font. As a result, `min-height` / `max-height` are too small until the window is resized.

**Cause (as far as I can tell):**
- `CdkTextareaAutosize` measures and caches the line height on the first `ngDoCheck` (`resizeToFitContent` → `_cacheTextareaLineHeight`, cloning the textarea with `rows=1`).
- `MatInput` applies `font: inherit` via the class `mat-mdc-form-field-input-control`, which is a *dynamic* host binding (`'[class.mat-mdc-form-field-input-control]': '_isInFormField'`).
- Host bindings are applied after `ngDoCheck` in the first change detection pass. So at measuring time the textarea (and its clone) still uses the UA default textarea font (Chrome: monospace 13.33px, `line-height: normal` ≈ 15px).
- The wrong value stays cached until a window `resize` clears it.

**Measured on the official docs example** (`cdkAutosizeMaxRows="5"`, actual line height 24px):

| Docs | Angular | measured line height | `max-height` |
|---|---|---|---|
| v14 | 14.0.0 | 18px (correct) | 90px |
| v15 | 15.1.1 | 15px | 75px |
| v17 | 17.3.0 | 15px | 75px |
| v19 | 19.2.6 | 15px | 75px |
| v21 | 21.2.11 | 15px | 75px |
| current | 22.2.1 | 15px | 75px (expected 120px) |

It started with v15, i.e. the switch to the MDC-based form field.

**Workaround:** a global style so the textarea inherits the font before the first measurement:
```css
textarea.cdk-textarea-autosize { font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; }
```

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz needed – the official docs example reproduces it:
https://material.angular.dev/cdk/text-field/examples ("Auto-resizing textarea")

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open the page above (fresh load, don't resize the window).
2. Select the textarea in DevTools and run:
   ```js
   ({ minHeight: $0.style.minHeight, maxHeight: $0.style.maxHeight, lineHeight: getComputedStyle($0).lineHeight })
   ```
   → `minHeight: "15px"`, `maxHeight: "75px"`, `lineHeight: "24px"`
3. Type more than 3 lines: the textarea starts scrolling after ~3 lines instead of 5.
4. Resize the browser window and run the snippet again → `minHeight: "24px"`, `maxHeight: "120px"` (correct).

For comparison, the same example on https://v14.material.angular.dev/cdk/text-field/examples measures correctly on first load.

### Expected Behavior

min-height / max-height are based on the actual line height of the textarea (24px → max-height: 120px for 5 rows) right after the first render.

### Actual Behavior

They are based on the UA default textarea font (15px → max-height: 75px) until the window is resized.

### Environment

- Angular 22.2.1
- CDK/Material 22.2.x
- Chrome (Version 154.0.8037.95 (64-Bit))
- Windows 11

Issues.Body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.28.2` → `11.28.5`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.5`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.5): pnpm 11.28.5 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.4...v11.28.5) This release reads cached registry metadata faster and makes `pnpm config get --global` ignore project settings. It also carries several security fixes for package archives, git dependencies, and config dependencies. ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - pnpm now verifies locked config dependencies against their registry before installing them. Config dependencies must come from an npm registry. The lockfile can no longer replace the integrity of a config dependency pinned with `version+integrity`. - Lockfile verification now checks the tarballs inside a `variations` resolution against the registry. A `name@version` lockfile entry with an empty `variations` resolution is now rejected. - `pnpm audit signatures` now verifies signatures against the integrity recorded in the lockfile. Packages without a recorded integrity cannot pass signature verification. - pnpm now rejects a git dependency whose lockfile repository is empty, begins with `-`, or contains a null byte. Git can no longer read such a value as a command-line option [pnpm/tasks#84](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/84). - A git dependency with a `#path:` subpath can no longer reach files outside the repository through a symlink in the subpath. - `pnpm pack`, `pnpm publish`, and installs of git and local directory dependencies now leave out files that a directory symlink or a `bundleDependencies` entry points to outside the package directory [pnpm/tasks#83](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/83) [pnpm/tasks#93](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/93). - `pnpm deploy` with `deployAllFiles` now rejects symlinks that point outside the package directory. Local package installs with this setting apply the same check. - pnpm no longer hangs on a package archive with a negative PAX record length or an entry of 4 GiB or more [pnpm/tasks#78](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/78) [pnpm/tasks#79](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/79). - Large package downloads and large files inside gzip and bzip2 package archives now use bounded memory during installation. Package manifests and archive metadata larger than 64 MiB are rejected. `pnpm publish` also rejects manifests and README files larger than 64 MiB in pre-built tarballs before reading them into memory. - Two URL or local path dependencies no longer share a virtual store directory when one URL has `+`, `#`, `:`, or `?` where the other has `/`. Such dependencies, including git dependencies pinned with `#`, now get a hash suffix on their directory name. - `pnpm licenses` now removes terminal control characters from package metadata in table output. - The warnings about ignored project `.npmrc` registry and auth settings no longer print the username and password of a URL-scoped key such as `//user:password@registry.example.com/:_authToken`. ##### Installing and resolving dependencies - Dependency resolution reads cached registry metadata faster. The metadata cache moved to `/v12/`, so the first install after upgrading downloads registry metadata again. A damaged cache entry is downloaded again, or reported as an error when `--offline` is set [#​13512](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13512). - `pnpm install` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a dependency uses a specifier with a protocol pnpm does not support, such as Yarn's `patch:`. pnpm linked such a dependency to a directory that does not exist [#​16590](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16590). - When a dependency moves an exact dependency of its own to an older version, a peer dependency that pnpm installed automatically now moves with it. Before, `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` kept the newer locked version of the peer, so the lockfile held two copies of it, for example two copies of `vue` [pnpm/tasks#61](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/61). - `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now keep the peer dependencies that `pnpm-lock.yaml` records for a package they did not update. A registry whose metadata disagrees with the package's `package.json`, for example by omitting `peerDependenciesMeta`, made `pnpm add` and `pnpm dedupe` write different lockfiles, so `pnpm dedupe --check` failed after `pnpm add` [#​16615](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16615). ##### Configuration - `pnpm config get` and `pnpm config list` with `--global` or `--location=global` now show only the global configuration. Both flags included the project's `.npmrc` before. `--location=global` also included the project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `pnpm config get --global` failed when the global bin directory was not in PATH [#​16598](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16598). - pnpm now prints config warnings, such as an unset environment variable in `.npmrc`, when loading the config fails. - pnpm now fails when `httpProxy` or `httpsProxy` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global configuration is not a string. - `pnpm dlx` now uses the `release` entry of `nodeDownloadMirrors` from the workspace configuration when downloading Node.js runtimes [#​11281](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11281). Mirrors for other channels, such as `rc` and `nightly`, still apply only from the global configuration. ##### Commands - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now forward `--config.*` command-line flags to the install started by `verifyDepsBeforeRun` [pnpm/tasks#60](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/60). - `pnpm dlx` with `--package` but no command now fails with `'pnpm dlx' requires a command to run`. Before, it installed the package and then crashed trying to run an empty command. - `pnpm unpublish @` now deletes the tarball under the registry's path when the registry is served under one, such as Gitea's npm registry. It used to send the delete to the host root and report success without removing the version [#​16568](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16568). It also no longer mistakes a sibling path such as `/npm-mirror/` for the registry path `/npm/` [pnpm/tasks#94](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/94). - The interactive `pnpm audit --fix` picker now shows each patched version with the `saveExact` and `savePrefix` style that the override is written with [#​13209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13209). - `pnpm list` now reports the correct package paths when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​9593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9593). - `pnpm setup` now puts `$PNPM_HOME/bin` first on `PATH` in login shells that inherited it further down, such as the VS Code terminal on macOS. Before, another `node` took precedence over the one installed by `pnpm runtime set node -g`. Run `pnpm setup` again to update the block in your shell config [#​16635](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16635). - `pnpm setup` now names the shell config file even if it is already up to date [#​16608](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16608). ##### Output and messages - A warning about a project's `devEngines` or `packageManager` pin is now printed to stderr. A command such as `pnpm cache path` or `pnpm list --json` keeps only its own output on stdout [#​16584](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16584). - The warning for a non-root `resolutions` field now points at the `overrides` field in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​11757](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11757). #### Platinum Sponsors

### [`v11.28.4`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.4): pnpm 11.28.4 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.3...v11.28.4) pnpm 11.28.4 fixes two ways credentials could leak, makes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accept several lockfiles it rejected, warns when an optional dependency cannot be fetched, and stops `pnpm self-update` from installing a second pnpm next to a Homebrew one. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm login` no longer forwards credentials in its request body to another origin during redirects. - The error for a tarball that fails its integrity check no longer prints credentials, query strings, or fragments from the tarball URL. ##### Installing packages - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now succeeds in a project with no dependencies when `pnpm-lock.yaml` records only the pinned pnpm version. Other commands write such a lockfile when they run before the first install. A lockfile missing the `---` line after that section is accepted too [#​16477](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16477). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` again succeeds when a workspace project recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` has no directory, such as a project left out of a Docker build context. It still fails if the project's directory exists without a `package.json` [#​16453](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16453). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` for a workspace project that declares `dependenciesMeta` and whose dependencies are all workspace links. pnpm now records that project's `dependenciesMeta` in `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​16457](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16457). - Fixed frozen installs replacing a hoisted dependency with a workspace package of the same name. A later `pnpm dedupe` then removed the hoisted link [#​16485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16485). - With `enableGlobalVirtualStore` on, scripts can run entry points that a CommonJS require hook loads again, such as `ts-node index.ts`. They failed with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on Node.js versions without built-in TypeScript support [#​16436](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16436). ##### Optional dependencies - `pnpm install` now prints a warning with the error when an optional dependency cannot be fetched and is skipped. The skipped package is no longer linked into `node_modules` as a broken symlink or listed among the added dependencies. The `pnpm:skipped-optional-dependency` log reports the skip with the `fetch_failure` reason [#​16514](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16514). - When an optional dependency fails to build, pnpm now removes its link from `node_modules`. A repeat `pnpm install` then reports "Already up to date" and no longer reruns the failing build [#​16468](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16468). - Fixed frozen installs creating symlinks to the working directory for skipped optional dependencies and unresolved peer dependencies [#​16454](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16454). ##### Hoisted node_modules - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install now keeps the packages of the workspace projects an earlier install put in `node_modules`. This also covers the install that `pnpm --filter run` and `pnpm --filter exec` start before the command. Before, these installs removed every package that only the unselected projects needed [#​16483](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16483). A filtered install of a workspace project also no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` after a filtered install of another project. - `pnpm install` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` now refreshes directories supplied by custom fetchers when reinstalling. ##### Speed and network - pnpm now revalidates cached registry metadata with a conditional request, so the registry can answer `304 Not Modified`. Before, pnpm downloaded the whole document again for registries whose responses forbid caching, such as `Cache-Control: no-store` [#​16528](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16528), and for packages published within `minimumReleaseAge` [#​16506](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16506). - A fetch timeout while other downloads from the same host are still running now lowers concurrency for that host to one connection. Retries of that request, and later downloads from that host, use the lower concurrency. Other hosts keep the configured concurrency [#​12791](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12791). ##### Running scripts - Scripts run without a terminal no longer start a second `sh` each. One watchdog per pnpm command now ends every script's process group if pnpm is killed, so `pnpm -r run` across many projects starts half as many processes [#​16489](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16489). - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now warn and run the command when the install that `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starts fails. This lets scripts run in sandboxes where pnpm cannot install, such as containers with a read-only store or no network [#​15173](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15173). - A filtered `pnpm run` or `pnpm exec` now finds dependencies out of date when a workspace dependency of a selected project has no `node_modules` directory, as after a filtered install. With `verifyDepsBeforeRun: install`, pnpm installs that dependency before running the command [pnpm/tasks#45](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/45). - `pnpm rebuild` and `pnpm approve-builds` refresh command launchers when a build changes a command's interpreter or replaces it with a native executable. Dependent packages' build scripts use the refreshed launchers. ##### Updating pnpm - `pnpm self-update` now fails for Homebrew-installed pnpm and prints the `brew upgrade` command for the installed formula, such as `brew upgrade pnpm` or `brew upgrade pnpm@11`. It used to install a second copy of pnpm that the Homebrew one kept shadowing [#​16547](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16547). - On Windows, `pnpm self-update` now replaces a `pnpm.exe` left in `PNPM_HOME` or in `PNPM_HOME\bin`. In `PNPM_HOME`, that executable kept running the old version after a successful update. In `PNPM_HOME\bin`, the update failed with `EPERM`. If the executable was in `PNPM_HOME`, `self-update` now asks you to run `pnpm setup` [#​9094](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9094). - pnpm can now switch to a `packageManager` version below 11 on x64 musl Linux, such as Alpine [#​16467](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16467). - A `devEngines.packageManager` range now records the running pnpm in `pnpm-lock.yaml` only if it meets `minimumReleaseAge`. Otherwise pnpm records the newest version in the range that meets it. If no version in the range does, pnpm still records the running pnpm [#​16431](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16431). ##### Filtering, settings, and other commands - The `[]` filter selector works again with Git 2.24 through 2.27 [#​16561](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16561). With Git older than 2.24, the selector now fails with an error that names the required Git version. - Package-name filters now support `?` to match one character [#​2817](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2817). - `pnpm -r pkg get` now reports every selected project when several share a package name. Projects with the same name are keyed by their directory relative to the workspace root. Before, only one of them appeared in the output. - pnpm now reports an `INVALID_SETTING` error when `allowUnusedPatches` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is not a boolean, or when `ignoredOptionalDependencies` or `requiredScripts` is not an array of strings. A quoted `allowUnusedPatches` value such as `"false"` was treated as `true`. - `pnpm store path`, `pnpm store status`, and other commands that look up the default store no longer fail when the current directory is not writable. pnpm now uses the store in the pnpm home directory in that case [#​16554](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16554). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.3`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.3): pnpm 11.28.3 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.2...v11.28.3) pnpm 11.28.3 updates `undici` to clear a security advisory, fixes "database disk image is malformed" errors when several pnpm processes share a store, and makes packages, catalogs, projects, and commands named like `constructor` work. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - pnpm now ships `undici` 7.29.1, so security scans of pnpm no longer report [GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v). - pnpm no longer fails with "database disk image is malformed" or reads stale store entries while another pnpm process writes to the same store. - Names that match built-in JavaScript object properties, such as `constructor`, `toString`, or `__proto__`, now work like any other name. pnpm crashed, wrote a wrong lockfile, or silently skipped such names in: - `pnpm add`, `pnpm install`, and `pnpm import`, for dependencies, peer dependencies, and `file:` dependencies that point to a directory named `constructor`. - Catalog entries and catalog names. Pruning unused entries crashed, and a new catalog named `toString` was not written. - Workspace projects, project directories, and files inside injected packages. - Registry prefixes and override version references such as `$toString`. - Hoisting, `pnpm list`, and `pnpm why`. - Command names. `pnpm constructor` runs the `constructor` script like any other unknown command, and `pnpm help constructor` no longer crashes. - Resolving through a pnpr server when a project lives in a directory named `constructor`. - `pnpm install` no longer re-resolves an up-to-date lockfile on every run when a patched package is a peer in a peer cycle [#​16418](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16418). - POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build, where the system default path holds none of the utilities they call. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​16377](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16377). - In a project that pins another pnpm version, pnpm now passes a command with an option it does not know to the pinned version. Before, `pnpm install --auto-dedupe` failed with "Unknown option" even though the pinned pnpm supports it [#​16353](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16353). - pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_ALLOW_BUILDS` when `allowBuilds` is not an object or one of its values is not `true`, `false`, or a string. Such values used to be ignored silently. - Removing a dependency whose bins are declared through `directories.bin` no longer leaves broken shims in `node_modules/.bin`. - A custom resolver's `shouldRefreshResolution` hook that rejects no longer crashes pnpm with an unhandled rejection when another hook has already asked for a refresh. ##### Updating dependencies - When `minimumReleaseAge` hides the version that `latest` points to, pnpm now falls back to a prerelease of the same major before a stable version of an older major. A stable version of the same major is still preferred. For example, while a new `1.0.0` is too new, pnpm picks `1.0.0-beta.4` rather than an old `0.0.1` [#​16388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16388). - `pnpm --filter update ` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PACKAGE_IN_DEPENDENCIES` when the selected projects do not depend on ``, also in a workspace with a shared lockfile and a root project. It used to exit successfully. - `pnpm audit --fix` now updates vulnerable packages in a single project that sets `updateConfig.ignoreDependencies`. It used to leave them on the vulnerable version. - `pnpm update --global` now removes hard-linked executables from `PNPM_HOME` when migrating packages from the old global layout [#​16420](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16420). - Updating a pinned GitHub Action now rewrites the version in its `# vX.Y.Z` comment even when the action name contains the same version text. The action name used to change while the comment kept the old version. ##### Workspaces and deploy - `pnpm deploy` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` in a workspace with `injectWorkspacePackages: true` when a workspace package also lists its peer dependency as a dev dependency [#​16375](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16375). - `pnpm deploy` no longer copies the workspace root's `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` fields into the deployed `package.json` [#​16403](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16403). - `--filter` fixes: - A `...pkg...` selector combined with another dependents selector, such as `--filter ...a --filter ...b...`, no longer adds the dependencies of the other selector's dependents. - `--filter "[]"` now detects changes in projects whose directory names contain non-ASCII characters. The change used to be credited to the parent project. ##### Running scripts - After relaying a signal to a script, pnpm keeps waiting for a process in the script's process group whose main thread has exited while its other threads still run. Linux reports such a process as a zombie, so the wait used to end before those threads finished [pnpm/tasks#56](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/56). - A lifecycle script run with `unsafePerm: false` now fails with an error when pnpm cannot create `node_modules/.tmp`. It used to hang. - `pnpm run` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer crashes with an unhandled rejection when a lockfile it did not need to compare fails to load. - `pnpm run -r` now closes the collapsible CI log section of a project whose script fails, so the output of later projects is no longer nested inside it. - `pnpm run --resume-from` no longer crashes when a saved run state file contains `null`. ##### Store - `pnpm store prune` now removes the packages that only expired `pnpm dlx` cache entries used, as long as the store still has another registered project. They used to stay until the next `pnpm store prune` [#​16383](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16383). - `pnpm store prune` now stops with an error when it cannot read a project directory for a reason other than the directory missing, such as a permission error. It used to skip the directory. ##### Publishing and registry output - `pnpm publish` now includes bare `README` files and README files with Markdown extensions such as `readme.markdown` in registry metadata [#​12704](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12704). - `pnpm pack-app` now accepts an entry file or output directory inside the project whose name starts with two dots, such as `..build/entry.cjs`. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_PACK_APP_ENTRY_OUTSIDE_PROJECT`. - Registry error messages now always say "(response body truncated)" when pnpm cut the response body short. The marker was missing when the body was cut at exactly 64 KiB. #### Platinum Sponsors

  - `Client`.

  - One server object with a new stateless transport per request (`const server = new McpServer(...)` outside the handler, `await server.connect(transport)` inside it): the second HTTP request the process receives fails, and so does every later one. `connect()` rejects with an `SdkError` of code `ALREADY_CONNECTED`. If the handler closes the transport when the response ends, requests that arrive one after the other still work and a request that overlaps another one fails. Change: move `new McpServer(...)` and its registrations into the handler.

Create a new transport per request.`, and `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` answers `500`. Change: build the server and the transport inside the handler and connect them there.

This release fixes two ways `pnpm install` could fail, runs tools of any Rust release through `pnx`, and treats `registry.npmjs.com` as an alias of the npm registry.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install` no longer fails when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version. pnpm warns and continues. A registry mirror that has not synced a release no longer blocks the commands of a project pinned to it.

- `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD` when `node_modules/.bin` holds a shim that another user created, if everyone can already execute it and it is not world-writable. This happens when several users share one checkout.

- pnpm now treats `https://registry.npmjs.com/` as an alias of `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Registry requests, credentials, and trusted publishing use the canonical hostname.

- `pnx --package=rust@<channel> <tool>` runs a tool of that Rust release, for example `pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-01-01 cargo build`. pnpm installs the release with the components and targets from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the target of each `--target` argument.

### [`v12.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.0): pnpm 12.11.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.10.1...v12.11.0)

This release adds Rust toolchain management, links the agent skills that dependencies ship, adds the `permissions` setting, and keeps the colors of streamed script output.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm install` now links the agent skills that direct dependencies ship under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` into the project's agent skill directories, such as `.claude/skills`. A package's skills are linked only after you approve them with `pnpm approve`. The `skills.dirs` setting chooses the directories [pnpm/rfcs#35](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/35).

  Added the `permissions` setting, which records what each dependency may do. Its `build` capability works like `allowBuilds` and takes precedence over it. `pnpm approve-builds` writes to `permissions` when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` already has it, and to `allowBuilds` otherwise.

  Added `pnpm permissions`, which lists the granted and denied permissions and the packages awaiting approval. `pnpm approve` reviews build scripts and agent skills in one prompt [pnpm/rfcs#36](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/36).

- pnpm now installs and runs Rust toolchains.

  - With `cargo.enabled`, `pnpm install` installs the toolchain named in `rust-toolchain.toml`. pnpm verifies the release signature, stores the toolchain once per machine, and links it into `.pnpm/rust`. `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` put its `cargo` and `rustc` on the `PATH`.
  - `pnpm add -g rust@<channel>` installs a toolchain globally. The `cargo` and `rustc` commands run it outside projects that pin their own. `pnpm update -g`, `pnpm ls -g`, and `pnpm remove -g` manage it like any global package.
  - In a project, `pnpm add rust@<channel>` pins the toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
  - `pnpm shim add rust` adds project-aware shims for `cargo`, `rustc`, and the other Rust tools. In a project with a `rust-toolchain.toml`, they run the toolchain the file names and install it on first use.
